customManagers.description: govulncheck pin in ci.yml's env: block — invisible to the github-actions manager, which only reads uses: refs, not env: values.

flux-schema plugin pin in validate-manifests.sh. Nothing else proposes bumps to it: it is independent of the mise-managed flux2 CLI (a `flux plugin`, versioned separately by fluxcd/flux-schema's own releases), and ci.yml no longer carries a duplicate to key off.

packageRules.description: fluxcd/flux-schema tags its GitHub releases with a leading v (e.g. v0.12.1); extractVersion strips it before comparing against SCHEMA_PLUGIN_VERSION's bare-number form. extractVersion is illegal inside a customManager itself (Renovate ignores it there), so it must live in a separate packageRule matched on the same synthetic depName.

Direct deps shared with the imported kure are never proposed here: launcher must not lead the kure release it imports (MVS pulls launcher up automatically, so only the 'ahead' direction needs control — see AGENTS.md § 'Shared dependencies with kure'). CI enforces this via site/scripts/check-kure-dep-sync.sh; this list mirrors that guard's current shared-direct set and must be updated together with go.mod changes that add or drop a shared direct dep — a dep missing here is still caught by the CI guard, just as a red PR instead of never being proposed. Correct sequence for these: land the kure bump, cut a kure release, bump the go-kure/kure require, take the shared dep together.

Keep go.mod's go directive, versions.yaml's go.current and README.md's shields.io badge in sync with mise.toml's go pin (sync-go-version.sh, checked by make check-go-version and by sync-versions.sh check's validate_gomod respectively), and regenerate the golangci-lint pins in Makefile/ci.yml/docs (sync-tool-versions.sh), on the bot's own branch after any gomod or mise bump. mise.toml is the only copy Renovate's mise datasource actually updates; the rest are plain strings a human (or this task) must keep in step. A mise-only Go bump previously left go.mod, versions.yaml and README.md all behind with no postUpgradeTasks command to fix any of them, and CI's validate job fails on drift for any of these (go-kure/kure#734, the same defect class here). Both scripts are no-ops when nothing derived changes, so matching both managers is safe.

Keep docs/github-workflows.md's govulncheck version mention in sync with the GOVULNCHECK_VERSION pin the customManager above bumps in ci.yml. Scoped to that customManager specifically, not just by depName: golang.org/x/vuln is also a real go.mod dependency, and without matchManagers a gomod-sourced bump of it would match here too — postUpgradeTasks has no merge semantics, so this rule's commands would silently replace the gomod/mise rule's own postUpgradeTasks, reintroducing the drift that rule exists to prevent.
